blocks.text: Can transcriptomic features of neutrophil extracellular trap formation predict prognosis across cancers?
69 initial biomarkers -> LASSO -> 24 non-zero genes -> correlation pruning -> 19-gene NETs score.
TCGA pan-cancer n=8,739 across 32 tumor types (6,117 training; 2,622 test), with CGGA n=651, METABRIC n=1,868 and GEO n=2,459 external data.
Higher NETs score tracked worse DSS, OS and PFI and remained independently associated with OS in the TCGA test cohort (HR=1.22, p=0.0070).
External cohorts supported prognostic value in glioma and LUAD, but not consistently in breast cancer or LUSC.
NETs activity correlated with EMT (R=0.7444), angiogenesis (R=0.5369) and cell cycle activity (R=0.3835); all p<0.0001.
MPO staining stratified outcomes in COAD, KIRC and LUAD, but not TNBC; MPO remained independent in COAD and KIRC.
A transcriptomic NETs-formation signature captures clinically relevant, tumor-type-specific prognosis and malignant biology; broader marker and cancer-type validation is still needed.
